description: Upstream projects and datasets whose new releases may add techniques Perdedor should check. Read by `perdedor upstream check`; see docs/UPSTREAM.md. `pinned` is the last reviewed revision (date = when it was pinned, released = when upstream published it).

upstreams.name: VMAware
upstreams.why: Largest actively maintained VM/sandbox detection library; its technique enum is the broadest list of tells Perdedor should be able to reproduce. Renamed from kernelwernel/VMAware.

upstreams.name: al-khaser
upstreams.why: The reference Windows anti-VM, anti-debug and anti-sandbox check suite that malware authors copy from. Moved from LordNoteworthy/al-khaser.

upstreams.name: Pafish
upstreams.why: The original sandbox-detection demonstrator. The repository is archived, so a change here is unexpected.

upstreams.name: InviZzzible
upstreams.why: Configurable evasion test tool from Check Point; its config/*.conf files list the checks with scores and countermeasures.

upstreams.name: Check Point Evasions encyclopedia
upstreams.why: The most complete public catalogue of sandbox, VM and debugger evasion techniques with signature recommendations (evasions.checkpoint.com).

out_of_scope.reason: APK and manifest malformations aimed at analysis tools; a property of the sample file, not of the device under test.
Describes how the sample itself is built (packing, obfuscation, disassembly tricks), not anything the analysis environment shows; nothing to test in a sandbox.
Blocks keyboard and mouse input to hinder an interactive debugger; changes system state and says nothing about the environment.
Moves the sample to another desktop to hide from an interactive debugger; changes system state.
An action the sample takes against monitoring or forensics (tampering, hiding, cleaning up), not a check of the environment; a sandbox records it as behaviour, and there is nothing read-only to test.
An action the sample takes against monitoring or forensics (tampering, hiding, cleaning up), not a check of the environment; a sandbox records it as behaviour, and there is nothing read-only to test.

upstreams.name: Unprotect Project
upstreams.why: Community database of malware evasion techniques mapped to ATT&CK and MBC; no public repository, so the technique index page is hashed and a change is a prompt to review the site.

upstreams.name: MITRE ATT&CK STIX data
upstreams.why: Authoritative technique and procedure-example data for T1497 (virtualization/sandbox evasion), T1622 (debugger evasion) and T1633 (mobile sandbox evasion); the check catalog maps its techniques to these ids.

upstreams.name: MITRE CTI repository
upstreams.why: The original ATT&CK STIX repository; it still publishes a release for each ATT&CK version, so it is a second signal for a new matrix version.

upstreams.name: Malware Behavior Catalog
upstreams.why: MBC behaviours B0001-B0037 (debugger and VM detection, sandbox detection, emulator detection) are referenced from the technique catalog.

upstreams.name: MBC STIX 2.1 data
upstreams.why: Machine-readable MBC; a new tag means new or renumbered behaviours.

upstreams.name: anti-emulator (Android)
upstreams.why: The classic Android emulator detection checks (QEMU files and drivers, telephony defaults, build properties) that the Android agent must pass.

upstreams.name: freeRASP for Android
upstreams.why: Widely deployed Android app-protection SDK; its threat callbacks list what apps check (root, hooks, emulator, debugger, developer mode).

upstreams.name: freeRASP for iOS
upstreams.why: iOS counterpart of freeRASP; the checks are in a binary framework, so only releases are watched.

upstreams.name: freeRASP for Flutter
upstreams.why: The Threat enum is the cross-platform list of freeRASP detections (Android and iOS).

upstreams.name: IOSSecuritySuite
upstreams.why: Open-source iOS jailbreak, emulator, debugger and reverse-engineering detection; defines the iOS checks the future iOS agent should resist.

upstreams.name: RootBeer
upstreams.why: The most used open-source Android root detection library; its checks are what apps run on a rooted analysis device.

upstreams.name: Android Native Root Detector
upstreams.why: Native-code root and hook detection for Android; watched for new detection ideas, no parser.

upstreams.name: OWASP MASTG
upstreams.why: Mobile security testing guide: the tests for root, emulator and tamper detection that app developers are told to implement. Renamed from OWASP/owasp-mastg.

upstreams.name: DRAKVUF
upstreams.why: The introspection engine CHIMERA runs; new plugins and options (cpuidmon, hidsim, altp2m changes) change what the sandbox can hide.

upstreams.name: DRAKVUF Sandbox
upstreams.why: The analysis pipeline built on DRAKVUF; its releases show how other deployments handle evasion and VM hardening.

upstreams.name: LibVMI
upstreams.why: VM introspection library under DRAKVUF; its last release is from 2020, so the master branch is tracked.

upstreams.name: Xen 4.19 releases
upstreams.why: The hypervisor CHIMERA runs (4.19 branch): new point releases carry security fixes and hypercall or CPUID behaviour changes. Tags RELEASE-4.19.N on the GitHub mirror.

upstreams.name: Xen security advisories
upstreams.why: The advisory index at xenbits.xen.org; a changed page means a new XSA to assess against the pinned Xen build.

upstreams.name: QEMU
upstreams.why: The device model behind Xen HVM guests: new releases change emulated devices, ACPI and SMBIOS strings that guests can fingerprint.

upstreams.name: systemd (systemd-detect-virt)
upstreams.why: systemd-detect-virt is what many Linux samples and tools call; virt.h lists the hypervisors and container runtimes it recognises.

upstreams.name: virt-what
upstreams.why: Shell tool that detects virtualization from CPUID, DMI and /proc; the release page is hashed (no public git mirror).

upstreams.name: capa rules (anti-analysis)
upstreams.why: Mandiant capa's anti-analysis rules (anti-vm, anti-debugging, anti-emulation) describe the evasion behaviours found in real samples.

upstreams.name: CAPE community signatures
upstreams.why: CAPE's antisandbox, antivm, antidebug and antiemu signatures list evasions seen in malware that a sandbox reports. Directory-wide commit tracking is noisy; the technique list is the useful part.

upstreams.name: VmwareHardenedLoader
upstreams.why: Open-source VMware hardening against detection; its patch list shows which tells defenders consider worth hiding.

upstreams.name: VMDE (Virtual Machine Detection Engine)
upstreams.why: Early VM detection engine; archived, kept as a historical reference.
